entries.title: a Rust function called only inside a macro is no longer reported as having no caller
entries.summary: The Rust grammar leaves a macro's arguments as tokens, so a function called only inside `assert_eq!`, `vec!`, `println!` or a test macro had no caller on record, and `get_dead_code_v2` reported it with no caller. Rust tests are written almost entirely inside such macros. The parser now reads those tokens, and the body of each `macro_rules!` arm: a name directly followed by a parenthesised group is a call of that name. Every tool that reads call references inherits it. An existing index is re-parsed once. Tokens cannot tell a call from a pattern, so `Some(y)` inside a macro is recorded too; the CHANGELOG lists the limits.

entries.title: a call through a receiver records the method, never the receiver
entries.summary: For a call written through a receiver, `t.Recv()`, the parser recorded the receiver's name in Go, Java, Rust, Ruby and C#. So a method called only that way read as never called, and `get_dead_code_v2` reported it with no caller; a function that shared a name with a receiver read as called. The parser now reads each grammar's own callee and member fields, and a callee it does not know records nothing. Every tool that reads call references inherits it. An existing index is re-parsed once. Some functions that were found only by a shared name are reported now, a few of them live; the CHANGELOG lists the measured cases.

entries.title: a name that starts or ends in a punctuation mark is matched where it is used
entries.summary: A name that ends or starts in a punctuation mark (Ruby and Elixir `valid?` and `save!`, Clojure `empty?` and `-main`) was never matched where it is used: every tool that asks whether text names a symbol wrapped the name in word boundaries, and a word boundary beside a mark exists only when a word character is on its other side. `get_dead_code_v2` reported such a function with no caller wherever its evidence was text, `get_blast_radius` did not find its uses, and the rename plan in `plan_refactoring` skipped them. The rule is one module now and each side of a name is decided by the name's own first or last character; a name with a word character at both ends is matched exactly as before. The CHANGELOG lists what the new rule no longer matches.

entries.title: dead code: a caller in another file is found without an import edge
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` no longer reports a function as having no caller when its only caller is in another file the import graph does not join to it. For a language that records no call reference the tool read the function's own file and its importers; a Clojure `:require`, an Elixir `alias`, an Erlang remote call, a Bash `source` and two C files sharing a header give the graph no such edge. A function still without a caller is now asked of every other text-read code file. The trade is toward not reporting: a function nothing calls is no longer reported when another code file names it in a comment, an Elixir `@spec`, an Erlang `-export` or a doc comment above a C prototype. The CHANGELOG lists every measured case in both directions.
